question.text: How many people will have applied to Kyrgyzstan's CEC to run in the January 2027 presidential election by the close of nominations (13 November 2026)?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the number of distinct persons from whom Kyrgyzstan's Central Commission for Elections and Referendums (CEC) received an application to be nominated as a candidate in the 27 January 2027 presidential election during the official nomination period — i.e., the CEC's final count of applications accepted in that period, which the CEC's [election calendar](https://shailoo.gov.kg/ru/election/vybory-yanvar-2027/schedule/) shows ending on 13 November 2026 (the CEC has also given 24:00 on 12 November 2026 as the cut-off for submitting applications; the CEC's final total controls either way). The answer is the final figure the CEC publishes after the nomination period on its [news page](https://shailoo.gov.kg/ru/news/) or its [2027 election section](https://shailoo.gov.kg/ru/vybory-prezidenta-kr-2027/); if the CEC states no aggregate figure, count the distinct persons on the CEC's list of citizens who submitted applications; if neither is available, use the figure the CEC gives to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). Party-nominated and self-nominated candidates both count, each person is counted once even if they file more than once, and a person whose application the CEC recorded counts even if it was later withdrawn or refused. A person whose documents the CEC declined to accept at intake does not count. For example, if the CEC reports that 17 citizens had submitted applications, the question resolves to 17.
question.fine_print: Where the CEC reports both the number of applications received and the number of applicants whose documents were confirmed compliant, the number of applications received is used. Later stages of the process — signature collection (deadline 8 December 2026), the 1 million som deposit and candidate registration (deadline 23 December 2026) — do not affect the answer. If the CEC's final figure appears later than 13 November 2026, the question resolves when it is published.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-30: The CEC news page (shailoo.gov.kg/ru/news) lists three presidential applicants, all self-nominated: Aimen Kasenov (his representative was registered on 16 October), Azamat Esenbekov (filed 27 October) and Syimyk Zhapykeev (filed 28 October). On 30 October the CEC registered representatives for Esenbekov and Zhapykeev. I found no fourth application on the page. [CEC news](https://shailoo.gov.kg/ru/news/)
- The CEC's own items give different cut-offs. The 27 October item says nominations run until 13 November; the 28 October item says applications close at 24:00 on 12 November. 24.kg quoted the CEC as saying "12 November at 00:00", which is ambiguous. [24.kg](https://24.kg/article/vybory-prezidenta-syjmyk-zhapykeev-vydvinul-svoyu-kandidaturu)
- I did not fetch the 2027 election section or the calendar page directly.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The latest confirmed count is 3, as of 28 to 30 October. I found no reports of new applications between 29 October and 2 November. There are about 10 days left.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-30: The CEC registered authorized representatives for Esenbekov and Zhapykeev. [CEC](https://shailoo.gov.kg/ru/news/)
- 2026-10-28: Zhapykeev, a former head of the Financial Police, became the third applicant. He first failed the state-language test and passed on a retake. He says he has already paid the 1 million som deposit. [24.kg](https://24.kg/article/vybory-prezidenta-syjmyk-zhapykeev-vydvinul-svoyu-kandidaturu), [economist.kg](https://economist.kg/vlast/2026/10/28/zhapykeev-vybory-prezidenta-2027/), [knews](https://knews.kg/2026/10/28/syjmyk-zhapykeev-obratilsya-v-tsik-s-zayavleniem-o-vydvizhenii-svoej-kandidatury-na-dolzhnost-prezidenta-kyrgyzstana)
- 2026-10-27: Esenbekov filed as a self-nominee. He also filed in 2021 and later withdrew. [economist.kg](https://economist.kg/vlast/2026/10/27/esenbekov-vybory-2027/)
- 2026-10-14: Kasenov filed the first application. [Azattyk](https://www.azattyqasia.org/a/predprinimatel-aymen-kasenov-snova-reshil-ballotirovatsya-v-prezidenty-kyrgyzstana/33876473.html)
- 2026-09-29: The CEC says a state-language certificate at "above intermediate" level is required **for registration**. The article does not say it must come with the initial application, so whether the test now gates filing itself is unconfirmed. Zhapykeev's sequence (test first, then filing) hints that it might. [economist.kg](https://economist.kg/vlast/2026/09/29/tsik-proverka-kandidatov-prezident/)
- 2026-08 onward: President Japarov says he will run. 24.kg reports he will not need to retake the language test. He had not filed as of 28 October. I found no news on whether a party will nominate him. [Kommersant](https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/8881424), [24.kg](https://24.kg/article/vybory-2027-sadyru-zhaparovu-ne-pridetsya-sdavat-test-po-gosyazyku)
- I found no evidence that Omurbek Suvanaliev has filed.

## 4. Base rates
- 2011: 83 applications, 67 self-nominated and 16 from parties (cited by 24.kg). [24.kg](https://24.kg/vlast/173075_vyiboryi_prezidenta_uvedomleniya_obnbspuchastii_podali_63nbspcheloveka/)
- 2017: 59 applications, 13 candidates registered. [OSCE](https://cdn.osce.org/sites/default/files/f/documents/0/3/346966.pdf), [Novaya Gazeta](https://novayagazeta.ru/articles/2017/08/07/73362-59-kandidatov)
- 2020-21: 65 people applied. 2 withdrew, leaving 63 notifications (62 self-nominated, 1 from a party), and 18 were registered. Under this question's rules the comparable figure is 65. [24.kg](https://24.kg/vlast/173075_vyiboryi_prezidenta_uvedomleniya_obnbspuchastii_podali_63nbspcheloveka/)
- The trend has been stable at roughly 59 to 83 applications per cycle. The 2026 pace is much slower: 3 applications after about five weeks. Past cycles bunched filings at the end of the window, but I could not find day-by-day counts from 2017 or 2020 to measure how big the late surge was. Possible reasons for the drop are tighter rules, such as the language test and electronic signature collection, and a less competitive political climate. These are not confirmed.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the markets provided (Kalshi markets on US, French, Argentine, Serbian and Navajo elections) match this question.
- I found no prediction market, Metaculus question or expert forecast on the number of Kyrgyz applicants.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Japarov's own filing is still to come. It will probably come late, and possibly through a party nomination, which would require a party congress.
- Suvanaliev and other figures who have said they will run may file.
- Party congresses to nominate candidates have not been reported yet.
- 12 November, 24:00: final deadline for applications. 13 November: the nomination stage closes. The CEC's final total is expected around 13 November.
- Things to watch: CEC running totals and Kyrgyztest sessions, since the number of people taking the test could signal how many will file.

- Omurbek Suvanaliev and Akai Kydyrov have signalled they will run but, per reports, have not filed.

## 4. Base rates (in past races most applications arrived at the very end)

**2020/21 early election** (nomination deadline 14 November 2020):
- 2020-11-13, morning: 24 applications. [Informburo](https://informburo.kz/novosti/na-dolzhnost-prezidenta-kyrgyzstana-pretenduyut-24-cheloveka.html)
- 2020-11-13, 20:30: 34 applications, one withdrawn. [24.kg](https://24.kg/english/173043_Presidential_elections_Final_day_for_accepting_applications_from_candidates)
- Final: 65 applications, 2 withdrawn, leaving 63 (62 self-nominated, 1 party). [24.kg](https://24.kg/vlast/173075_vyiboryi_prezidenta_uvedomleniya_obnbspuchastii_podali_63nbspcheloveka/)
- So roughly half of all filings came in the last 1.5 days.
- In that cycle the CEC reminded applicants to take the Kyrgyz-language test after filing, so the test did not gate filing then. [24.kg](https://24.kg/vlast/173361_vyiboryi_prezidenta_tsik_napominaet_kandidatam_onbspsdache_kyirgyiztesta/)

**2017** (deadline 1 August):
- 2017-07-27: 41 applicants (32 self-nominated, 9 party). [24.kg](https://24.kg/english/58630_Kyrgyzstan_has_41_presidential_candidates)
- Final count was 58 to 59: one report gives 47 self-nominated plus 11 party, and ODIHR gives 59 applications, of which 9 were withdrawn, 37 rejected and 13 registered. [OSCE](https://www.osce.org/files/f/documents/0/3/346966.pdf)

**Contrast with 2026:**
- In 2026 there were 3 filings after about five weeks. In 2017 there were 41 five days before the deadline, and in 2020 there were 24 one day before.
- The 2026 pace is far slower. The main difference I found is that the language test now appears to come before filing. Other possible factors are a more restrictive political climate and an incumbent running.
- This suggests the 2026 total will probably fall well below about 60, but I found no data that quantifies this.

## 5. Other forecasts

- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on this or a closely related question.
- None of the Kalshi markets supplied with the question match it. They cover the US, French, Argentine, Serbian and Navajo elections.

- Possible filings to watch for:
  - Japarov's own application, likely through self-nomination or a party.
  - Suvanaliev, Kydyrov and other declared hopefuls.
  - Any party nominations.
- 2026-11-12, 24:00: the application cut-off. The nomination stage closes on 13 November. [CEC calendar](https://shailoo.gov.kg/ru/election/vybory-yanvar-2027/schedule/)
- 2026-11-13 or 14: based on 2020 practice, expect a final total from the CEC or 24.kg on the day after the deadline.
- Later stages (signatures due 8 December, registration closes 23 December) do not affect the answer.

(b) The latest known value is 3 applicants (Kasenov, Esenbekov, Zhapykeev), all self-nominated, as of 28 to 30 October 2026 on the CEC news page.

(c) If nothing changed, the outcome would be 3. That is unrealistic, because Japarov himself is almost certain to file.

(d) The current trend is about 3 filings in 5 weeks, with 2 of them in the last week. Extrapolating the recent pace with mild acceleration gives roughly 6 to 10 by the deadline.

(e) Historical totals were 83 in 2011, 59 in 2017 and 65 in 2020-21. In those cycles many filings came early, so a 2026 pace of 3 after five weeks shows a structural break. The likely causes are the language test probably gating filing, the 1 million som deposit, electronic signatures and a repressive climate. A late surge of 5 to 15 is plausible. A return to around 60 is very unlikely.

(f) There are no markets or expert forecasts. Japarov's remark that "quite a few candidates" will register suggests a handful, perhaps 5 to 10 serious rivals.

(g) In a low scenario, only Japarov and one or two others file, for a total of about 5. In a high scenario, a last-week wave of self-nominees arrives because the language test is required only at registration, not at filing, and the total reaches 30 to 40.
